[[File:UK Foto9.jpg|thumb|Ursula Keller (2022)]]
'''Ursula Keller''' (born 21 June 1959) is a Swiss physicist. She has been a tenured physics professor at [[ETH Zurich]], [[Switzerland]] since 1993.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Head of Research |url=https://ulp.ethz.ch/people/kursula.html |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=Ultrafast Laser Physics |language=en}}</ref> A pioneer in ultrafast science and technology,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honors and Awards |url=https://ulp.ethz.ch/people/kursula/honors-awards.html |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=Ultrafast Laser Physics |language=en}}</ref> she is known for inventing the semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM), enabling passive mode-locking of lasers and revolutionizing ultrafast laser applications in science and industry.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-12 |title="Swiss Nobel Prize" for Ursula Keller |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2022/09/swiss-nobel-prize-for-ursula-keller.html |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=ETH Zurich |language=en}}</ref> Keller led the Swiss NCCR MUST program in ultrafast science (2010–2022),<ref>{{Cite web |title=NCCR MUST :: NCCR MUST :: About NCCR MUST |url=http://www.nccr-must.ch/home.html |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=www.nccr-must.ch}}</ref> co-founded several companies, including Time-Bandwidth Products <ref>{{Cite web |title=Time-Bandwidth Products AG |url=https://ethz.ch/en/industry/entrepreneurship/explore-startup-portraits-and-success-stories/exits/time-bandwidth.html |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=ETH Zurich |language=en |archive-date=22 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250222043215/https://ethz.ch/en/industry/entrepreneurship/explore-startup-portraits-and-success-stories/exits/time-bandwidth.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> (now part of Lumentum <ref>{{Cite web |title=Ultrafast Lasers {{!}} Lumentum Operations LLC |url=https://www.lumentum.com/en/commercial-lasers/products/ultrafast-lasers |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=www.lumentum.com |archive-date=27 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250227151705/https://www.lumentum.com/en/commercial-lasers/products/ultrafast-lasers |url-status=dead }}</ref>) and K2 Photonics,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-09 |title=K2 Photonics - Innovative dual-comb lasers |url=https://k2photonics.com |access-date=2024-11-28 |language=en-US}}</ref> and published a graduate textbook "Ultrafast Laser Physics" with Springer Verlag.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Keller |first1=Ursula |title=Ultrafast Lasers |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-82532-4  |series=Graduate Texts in Physics |date=2021 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-82532-4|bibcode=2021ulla.book.....K |isbn=978-3-030-82531-7 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> She is highly cited <ref name="Ursula Keller">{{Cite web |title=Ursula Keller |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=8B4xjdYAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> and received many prestigious awards. From 2012-2016 she was the founding president of the Women Professors Forum at ETH Zurich.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Women Professors Forum |url=https://eth-wpf.ch |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=Women Professors Forum |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
Ursula Keller grew up in a working-class family.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Role Model: Dr. Ursula Keller – We Shape Tech |url=https://weshape.tech/2024/09/30/role-model-dr-ursula-keller/ |access-date=2024-11-28 |language=en}}</ref> After graduating with a "diploma" degree in physics in 1984 from ETH Zurich, Switzerland, she continued her studies at [[Stanford University]], where she obtained a master's degree in 1987, and then continued with a doctorate in 1989 in applied physics. The topic of her studies was the development of a new technique for optical measurement of charge and voltage in GaAs type integrated circuits.

From 1989 to 1993, she started her independent research as a member of technical staff at [[Bell Labs|AT&T Bell Laboratories]] in Holmdel, New Jersey, where she conducted research on photonic switching, ultra-fast laser technology and semiconductor spectroscopy and developed a method for manufacturing ultra-short pulse lasers.

In 1993, she was appointed as a tenured associate Professor of Physics at the [[Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology]] in Zurich, becoming the school's first female Professor of Physics.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.letemps.ch/sciences/ursula-keller-lumiere-bout-laser|title=Ursula Keller a vu la lumière au bout du laser|last=Logean|first=Sylvie|date=2018-04-25|work=Le Temps|language=fr}}</ref> In October 1997, she became a full professor.

Her research areas are ultra-fast solid-state and semiconductor lasers, the development of reliable and functional instruments to generate extreme ultraviolet (EUV) X-rays and attosecond science. She developed the first method for generating ultra-fast light pulses known as [[semiconductor saturable-absorber mirror]]s (SESAMs), which have become a worldwide industry standard for cutting and welding in fields ranging from electronics and automotive industry to communications technology, medical diagnostics and surgery and have made myriad important contributions to the field of laser science since.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ulp.ethz.ch/group.html|title=The Group|website=ulp.ethz.ch|language=en|access-date=2019-10-23}}</ref> Dr. Keller’s earlier research into [[carrier envelope phase]] stabilization and [[frequency comb]] technology was integral to [[Theodor W. Hänsch]] and [[John L. Hall]]’s development of laser-based spectroscopy that garnered them the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ethw.org/Ursula_Keller|title=Ursula Keller - Engineering and Technology History Wiki|website=ethw.org|access-date=2019-10-23}}</ref>

Ursula Keller has published more than 500 peer-reviewed journal papers <ref>{{Cite web |title=Journal Articles |url=https://ulp.ethz.ch/publications/journal-articles.html |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=Ultrafast Laser Physics |language=en}}</ref> with total [[citation]] of more than 56000 and [[h-index]] of 123.<ref name="Ursula Keller"/> Her first SESAM review publication <ref>{{Cite web |title=Semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors (SESAM's) for femtosecond to nanosecond pulse generation in solid-state lasers |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=8B4xjdYAAAAJ&citation_for_view=8B4xjdYAAAAJ:u5HHmVD_uO8C |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> has cited by 2472 people (as on 28. November 2024).

Ursula Keller has patented several inventions in the field of ultra-fast lasers for industrial and medical applications.<ref name=":0" />

She is the creator of the Attoclock,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Attoclock |url=https://ulp.ethz.ch/research/attoclock.html |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=Ultrafast Laser Physics |language=en}}</ref> one of the most accurate time measurement devices in the world, which can record time intervals up to a few attoseconds, the billionth part of a billionth of a second.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.lesechos.fr/thema/0301638092604-des-impulsions-laser-ultrarapides-pour-lindustrie-et-la-medecine-2173742.php#Xtor=AD-6000|title=Des impulsions laser ultrarapides pour l'industrie et la médecine|last=Echos|first=Les|date=2018-05-03|website=lesechos.fr|language=fr|access-date=14 December 2018|archive-date=14 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214164045/https://www.lesechos.fr/thema/0301638092604-des-impulsions-laser-ultrarapides-pour-lindustrie-et-la-medecine-2173742.php#Xtor=AD-6000|url-status=dead}}</ref>

From 2010 to 2022,  Ursula Keller has been Director of the Swiss National Research Centre for Ultra-fast Molecular Sciences and Technologies (NCCR MUST),<ref>{{Cite web |title=NCCR MUST :: NCCR MUST :: About NCCR MUST |url=https://www.nccr-must.ch/home.html |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=www.nccr-must.ch}}</ref> funded by the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NCCR MUST |url=https://www.snf.ch/en/Hng0ctSyAPOwW5pa/page/researchinFocus/nccr/nccr-must |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) |language=de}}</ref>

Since 2014, she has been a member of the Research Council of the Swiss National Science Foundation.<ref name=":1" />

In 2018, Ursula Keller won the European Inventor Award in the "Lifetime Achievement ".<ref name=":0" /> In 2019, she was appointed as one of the leading experts that judges proposals for this award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.epo.org/learning-events/european-inventor/jury.html?|title=European Inventor Award: jury members|last=Office|first=European Patent|website=www.epo.org|language=en|access-date=2019-01-21}}</ref>

She won the IEEE Photonics Award<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=IEEE Photonics Award Recipients|url=https://www.ieee.org/about/awards/bios/photonics-recipients.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180505065723/https://www.ieee.org/about/awards/bios/photonics-recipients.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 May 2018|website=[[IEEE]]|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref> in 2018 and the IEEE Edison Medal<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=IEEE Edison Medal Recipients|url=https://www.ieee.org/about/awards/bios/edison-recipients.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905023223/https://www.ieee.org/about/awards/bios/edison-recipients.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 September 2018|website=[[IEEE]]|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref> in 2019.

She won the 2020 Gold Medal from the Society of Photo-Optical Instrumentation Engineers<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gold Medal Winner Ursula Keller Among SPIE Award Honorees|url=https://www.photonics.com/Articles/Gold_Medal_Winner_Ursula_Keller_Among_SPIE_Award/a65308|website=www.photonics.com|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref> and the 2020 Frederic Ives Medal / Jarus Quinn Prize<ref>{{Cite web|title=OSA Honors Ursula Keller with Highest Award|url=https://www.photonics.com/Articles/OSA_Honors_Ursula_Keller_with_Highest_Award/a65634|website=www.photonics.com|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref> from the Optical Society.

Ursula Keller engages for equal rights and better career opportunities of women in fields of [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics]]. She was director of a research programme of the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] from 2010 till 2022,<ref>{{Cite web |title=NCCR MUST :: NCCR MUST :: About NCCR MUST |url=https://www.nccr-must.ch/home.html |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=www.nccr-must.ch}}</ref> and was the founding president of the ''ETH Women Professors Forum.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.weizmann.ac.il/WomenInScience/women-science-award/recipients/prof-dr-ursula-keller|title=Prof. Dr. Ursula Keller {{!}} Women In Science|website=www.weizmann.ac.il|date=25 April 2017|access-date=2018-12-14|archive-date=12 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181012131002/http://www.weizmann.ac.il/WomenInScience/women-science-award/recipients/prof-dr-ursula-keller|url-status=dead}}</ref> In March 2019, in the context of the mobbing allegations against [[Marcella Carollo]], Ursula Keller denounced a "lack of leadership, gender discrimination and corruption at ETH Zurich" and claimed that the reason for the proposed dismissal of her colleague was "not primarily the mobbing allegations, but her gender".<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Interview of Ursula Keller with the Online Platform "Republik"|journal=Republik |date=22 March 2019 |url=https://www.republik.ch/2019/03/22/mit-einem-maennlichen-professor-waere-man-anders-umgesprungen|access-date=2020-05-10|last1=Aeschlimann |first1=Silvan |last2=Bühler |first2=Dennis |last3=Osswald |first3=Dominik }}</ref> In the same period, Ursula Keller has been formally reprimanded by ETH Zurich, including the mention of a possible dismissal in case of recurrence.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NZZ am Sonntag, May 11, 2019|url=https://nzzas.nzz.ch/schweiz/eth-droht-zweiter-professorin-ursula-keller-mit-entlassung-ld.1481168|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref> Two external investigations disproved the accusations that Ursula Keller made against ETH Zurich.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tagesanzeiger, July 11, 2019|url=https://www.tagesanzeiger.ch/zuerich/stadt/die-eth-sieht-sich-entlastet/story/15560187|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref> Otherwise, the Swiss Federal Audit Office recommended more transparency in the distribution of funds.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=2022-07-23 |title=Die Tragik der ersten Physik-Professorin |url=https://epaper.limmattalerzeitung.ch/article/1101311/1101311/2022-07-23/7/303874795 |access-date=2022-08-05 |website=Limmattaler Zeitung }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> The [[Federal Administrative Court (Switzerland)|Federal Administrative Court of Switzerland]] ruled in 2022, that the termination was unjustified due to a lack of objectively sufficient grounds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-06 |title=Judgment of the Federal Administrative Court |url=https://www.bvger.ch/media-releases/38d39308-f9ff-41df-875f-5bd6f2aa3561/en/urteil_a-4744-2019_web.pdf |access-date=2024-11-25 |website=Federal Administrative Court}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* 1998: Zeiss Research Award, "for her pioneering work on the generation of high-power, ultra-short laser pulses using solid-state lasers".<ref>{{Cite web |title=ZEISS Research Award |url=https://www.zeiss.com/corporate/en/about-zeiss/future/promotion/zeiss-research-award.html#accordionItem-681022382 |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=www.zeiss.com |language=en}}</ref>
* 2003: Fellow of [[Optica (society)|OSA]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ursula Keller {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Ursula_Keller |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>
* 2004: [[:de:Berthold Leibinger Innovationspreis|Berthold Leibinger Innovation Prize]] from the [[Berthold Leibinger Stiftung]] for her Semiconductor Saturable Absorber Mirror (SESAM) invention enabling industrial mode locked solid-state lasers
* 2008: Joseph Fraunhofer Award / Robert M. Burley Prize from [[The Optical Society]]  "For seminal contributions to the development and application of ultrafast lasers and notably pioneering work on semiconductor saturable absorber mode-locking."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Joseph Fraunhofer Award / Robert M. Burley Prize|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/fraunhoferburley/|website=The Optical Society}}</ref>
* 2013: Arthur L. Schawlow Award, Laser institute of America (LIA), LIA's highest achievement award <ref>{{Citation |title=Arthur L. Schawlow Award |date=2024-11-28 |work=Wikipedia |url=https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_L._Schawlow_Award |access-date=2024-11-28 |language=de}}</ref>
* 2014: [[Fellow of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] (IEEE), 2014<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ieee.org/2014Fellowclass|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213225100/http://www.ieee.org/2014Fellowclass|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 December 2013|title=2014 elevated fellow|website=IEEE Fellows Directory}}</ref> for contributions to [[Ultrashort pulse laser|ultrashort pulse]] mode locked [[Laser science|laser physics]] and technology
* 2015: [[Charles H. Townes|Charles Hard Townes]] Award from [[The Optical Society]] "For seminal contributions in the fields of octave-spanning lasers, frequency comb technology, and high repetition-rate ultrafast semiconductor disc lasers."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Charles Townes Award|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/charlestownes/|website=The Optical Society}}</ref>
* 2017: [[Weizmann Women & Science Award|Weizmann Women and Science Award]], "In recognition of her pioneering and seminal contributions to ultrafast lasers technology and important breakthroughs in attosecond science" <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.phys.ethz.ch/news-and-events/d-phys-news/2017/06/keller-weizmann-women-and-science-award.html|title=Ursula Keller receives Weizmann Women & Science Award|date=2017-06-07|website=www.phys.ethz.ch|language=en|access-date=2018-12-14}}</ref>
* 2018: [[European Inventor Award]] for laser technology in the category "Lifetime achievement."<ref>[http://www.euronews.com/2018/06/07/six-award-winning-inventors-changing-the-world ''Six award winning inventors changing the world.''] Euronews, 7 June 2018. Retrieved 7 June 2018.</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/pioneering-patents_swiss-physicist-wins-european-inventor-award-for-laser-technology/44175270|title=Swiss physicist wins European Inventor Award for laser technology|work=SWI swissinfo.ch|access-date=2018-06-08|language=en}}</ref>
* 2018: [[IEEE Photonics Award]],<ref name=":2" /> 
* 2019: [[IEEE Edison Medal]],<ref name=":3" /> 
* 2020: [[SPIE Gold Medal]], is the highest honor the Society bestows, "in recognition of career long pioneering contributions in ultrafast science"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://spie.org/news/ursula-keller-2020-spie-gold-medal |title=Ursula Keller: The 2020 SPIE Gold Medal |website=[[SPIE]] |date=November 13, 2019 |access-date=November 26, 2019}}</ref>
* 2020: [[Frederic Ives Medal]]/Quinn Prize, which recognises overall distinction in Optics, from [[The Optical Society]] "For fundamental contributions to ultrafast lasers technology, especially the development of high peak and average power oscillators and important breakthroughs in attosecond science" <ref>{{Cite web|title=Frederic Ives Medal / Jarus W. Quinn Prize|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/ivesquinn/|website=The Optical Society|access-date=10 May 2020}}</ref>
* 2021: Elected as an international member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], USA<ref>{{Cite web|title=2021 NAS Election|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2021-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426172730/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2021-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 April 2021|access-date=2021-05-17|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>
* 2022: [[Marcel Benoist Prize]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past laureates – Marcel Benoist Foundation |url=https://marcel-benoist.ch/en/past-laureates/ |access-date=2024-11-28 |website=marcel-benoist.ch}}</ref> which has been dubbed the "Swiss Nobel Prize"
* 2025: Foreign Member of the [[Royal Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=2025-05-22 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
* 2026: Elected as an international member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]], USA,<ref>{{Cite web|title=National Academy of Engineering Elects 130 Members and 28 International Members|url=https://www.nae.edu/345149/NAENewClass2026|date=February 10, 2026|access-date=2026-02-10}}</ref> for "contributions to ultrafast lasers and attosecond technologies"
